description: Every tool POST /mcp offers. Written by scripts/mcp_json.sh from the registered tools; do not edit by hand. A key sees the tools its role allows (adminOnly ones need an admin key), and a tool whose feature is switched off answers like one that does not exist. route is the HTTP route the tool stands for, with the same rules; http_only are the routes a key may call that have no tool, and why.

http_only.reason: The MCP reference itself; tools/list gives the same list.
The API reference itself; GET /api/mcp.json is the MCP one.
Sign-in: managed from a browser, not by agents.
Sign-in: managed from a browser, not by agents.
File bytes: MCP messages are JSON, and clients cap their size. files_start_upload says where to send each piece, with the same key.
Ends a browser session; a key has none to end.
The browser's own activity reports (track.js), not an action.

tools.description: The account this API key belongs to, the role it acts with (role -- never higher than the key's own scope), and the account's own role.
tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Who am I

tools.description: People with an active account, a page at a time: id and display name. Use the id wherever another tool asks for a user. next is the offset of the following page, or null on the last one.

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next value of the previous page.

tools.name: list_team
tools.title: List team

tools.description: Accounts, a page at a time, including disabled ones, with each one's role and which is the owner. next is the offset of the following page, or null on the last one.

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next value of the previous page.

tools.name: admin_list_users
tools.title: List users (admin)

tools.description: Switch an account off (disabled: true) or back on (false). Disabling signs it out everywhere and voids its live login link; its API keys stop working while it is off. Reversible. The owner and your own account cannot be disabled.

user_id.description: The account's id, from list_team or admin_list_users.

tools.name: admin_set_user_disabled
tools.title: Disable or enable a user (admin)

tools.description: For an account that may be compromised: ends every session and voids its live login link and every API key it holds, at once. The account stays enabled; someone with a browser session must issue a new login link to let its owner back in. The owner and your own account cannot be revoked.

user_id.description: The account's id, from list_team or admin_list_users.

tools.name: admin_revoke_access
tools.title: Revoke a user's access (admin)

tools.description: Change your own display name (1-80 characters). expect, when given, is the name you think it has now; if someone changed it meanwhile the rename is refused with the current name, so nothing is overwritten unseen.

expect.description: The current name, from whoami. Optional.

tools.name: rename_account
tools.title: Rename your account

tools.description: Replace your changed keyboard shortcuts: action name to binding, such as "search": "Mod+K" (Mod is Cmd on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere). Send the whole set; an empty binding switches a key off, and {} puts every key back to its default. whoami shows the current set.
tools.name: set_shortcuts
tools.title: Change your keyboard shortcuts

tools.description: Replace your whole list of color themes (1 to 40) and pick the one you use. themes: null goes back to following the app's defaults. A theme is the Theme schema in the API reference (config/openapi.json): id, name, mode light|dark, accent, second, and optional colors as #rrggbb. whoami shows the current list.
tools.name: set_themes
tools.title: Replace your own themes

tools.description: Switch to another theme from your list (or the defaults), by its id.
tools.name: set_theme
tools.title: Pick your theme

tools.description: The theme list everyone without their own list sees. themes is null while the built-in ones apply.
tools.name: admin_get_theme_defaults
tools.title: Default themes (admin)

tools.description: Replace the theme list everyone without their own list sees, 1 to 40 themes in the Theme schema of the API reference. null puts the built-in themes back.
tools.name: admin_set_theme_defaults
tools.title: Replace the default themes (admin)

tools.description: Your uploaded files, a page at a time: id, name, type, size, state (uploading or ready) and when. next is the offset of the following page, or null on the last one.

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next value of the previous page.

tools.name: files_list
tools.title: List your files

tools.description: One file: its details, and for an unfinished upload how many pieces have arrived (received), which is where to resume.

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_get
tools.title: One of your files

tools.description: Reserve room for a file and get where to send it. The bytes do not go through MCP: POST each piece of chunk_bytes bytes (the last may be shorter), in order from index 0, as the raw body (Content-Type: application/octet-stream) to chunk_url with {index} filled in and the same Authorization: Bearer header this MCP connection uses. curl is a shell recipe that does all of it. Then call files_finish_upload.

name.description: The file's name, as it should be shown.

type.description: Its media type, such as application/pdf. Optional.

tools.name: files_start_upload
tools.title: Start uploading a file

tools.description: Seal an upload once every piece has arrived; the file is then ready to download. Asked again, it answers the same. If pieces are missing it says how many arrived (received).

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_finish_upload
tools.title: Finish an upload

tools.description: The address of one of your files. GET it over HTTP with the same Authorization: Bearer header this MCP connection uses; the bytes do not come through MCP.

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_download_url
tools.title: Where to download a file

tools.description: Give one of your files a new name. expect, when given, is the name you think it has now; a rename made meanwhile is refused with the current name.

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_rename
tools.title: Rename a file

tools.description: Move one of your files to the bin. files_restore brings it back for a while; after that it is gone.

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_delete
tools.title: Delete a file

tools.description: Bring back a file you deleted, while it is still in the bin and your storage quota has room.

file_id.description: The file's id, from files_list or files_start_upload.

tools.name: files_restore
tools.title: Restore a deleted file

tools.description: How many bytes your files use, and your quota (0 is no limit).
tools.name: my_storage
tools.title: Your storage

tools.description: Every account's files, a page at a time, with whose each one is (user_id, user_name). next is the offset of the following page, or null on the last one.

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next value of the previous page.

tools.name: admin_list_files
tools.title: List everyone's files (admin)

tools.description: How many bytes everyone's files use together, and the disk's free and total bytes where the system says.
tools.name: admin_storage
tools.title: Storage for everyone (admin)

tools.description: Group invite links, a page at a time: label, places used and left, expiry, and whether each still works. The links themselves are never shown again after creation. next is the offset of the following page, or null on the last one.

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next value of the previous page.

tools.name: admin_list_invite_links
tools.title: List invite links (admin)

tools.description: Stop an invite link from letting anyone else join or sign in through it. Accounts it already made keep working. Cannot be switched back on.
tools.name: admin_revoke_invite_link
tools.title: Switch off an invite link (admin)

transport: Streamable HTTP, stateless: one JSON-RPC message per POST, a JSON reply
